policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'behold, he was making' is compatible with both the separate qere pronoun and the ketiv suffix construction, and no mapped textual note distinguishes them; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV 'do that which is evil' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms, and no mapped textual note decides the unit; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV explicitly has the singular 'a perpetual hissing', distinguishing the ketiv singular form from the qere plural.
ASV explicitly renders 'a pit', distinguishing the qere שׁוּחָה from the ketiv שיחה.
ASV's jussive wording 'let them be overthrown' distinguishes the qere וְיִהְיוּ from the ketiv והיו; the Hebrew gloss 'made to stumble' confirms the predicate's sense without favoring the ketiv.
